summary: Phase S3 correctness re-audit passes. The remediation closes all seven prior blockers: the public service composes with one high-level port implemented by both adapters; the Drizzle adapter is bound to an authenticated school and actor and executes through TenantDB; composite database ownership plus immutable retarget checks protect card, review, evidence, state, placement, and commit identity; a real PGlite duplicate race resolves to one applied and one replayed receipt; calibration approval requires positive volume, improving evaluation, complete provenance, passing gates, and matching human/audit actors; UUID and digest contracts align across adapters; placement and calibration natural uniqueness are restored; and focused executable coverage exceeds 80 percent for every metric.
nonblocking_findings: The successful focused rerun selected the nine mastery-persistence test files and passed 110/110 assertions. The recorded 10-file 118/118 aggregate in commit 40a9e3b3 additionally includes the separate eight-assertion tenant-coverage slice.

A live migration-ledger doctor remains environment-gated because neither DIRECT_DATABASE_URL nor DATABASE_URL is configured. This does not weaken the physical PGlite migration, snapshot-chain, journal, sentinel, or ownership-constraint evidence.
The repository worktree contains extensive unrelated concurrent changes. This audit reviewed only the committed Phase S3 mastery/domain/database slice and changes only this audit artifact.
Browser runtime verification is not applicable: Phase S3 changes package, schema, SQL, test, and Measure files only and exposes no route, component, or user-visible UI.
evidence: Production composition is unified: commitMasteryEvidence validates the single strict Zod command and delegates to MasteryPersistencePort; createInMemoryMasteryPersistence and createDrizzleMasteryPersistence both implement readSnapshot, commitMasteryEvidence, and approveMasteryCalibration.

Tenant and owner integrity is real rather than payload-only: the Drizzle adapter requires tenant.schoolId and actorId, lazily creates and reuses createTenantDB, rejects foreign school/actor input before mutation, and migration 0028 adds composite users, cards, reviews, and evidence ownership constraints with fail-closed preflight checks.

Immutable CAS is enforced by persisted owner/natural-key comparison before revision writes, composite foreign keys, and unique natural keys; adversarial PGlite cases reject card/state retargeting and preserve the pre-operation snapshot.

The Drizzle adversarial suite issues simultaneous identical calls through two independently constructed adapters against PGlite and proves one applied plus one replayed stable receipt with exactly one commit and review; stale revisions remain typed, retryable, and atomic.

Calibration governance is carried through the public contract and stored record: positive review/student/training/holdout counts, count reconciliation, improving log loss, literal passing gates, model weights and version provenance, explicit approval, and matching approver/audit actor are validated before transaction execution.

Persisted school and record IDs are UUID-constrained while user-backed student and actor IDs remain bounded opaque text. Both adapters derive the same canonical SHA-256 request identity, deterministic UUID commit ID, result digest, revisions, and record IDs.
Schema, SQL, migration, and tests restore placement uniqueness on school/student/objective/graph release/evidence type and calibration uniqueness on school/domain/age band/parameter version.

Commit 40a9e3b3 records focused executable coverage of 90.6 percent statements, 80.76 percent branches, 100 percent functions, and 92.18 percent lines across the service, in-memory adapter, and Drizzle adapter.
Current targeted rerun passes nine files and 110/110 mastery-persistence assertions; the committed aggregate adds tenant coverage for 10 files and 118/118 assertions.
Graph Caller Check passes: the remediated persistence symbols are additive/new within the mastery facade and no non-additive pre-existing caller signature was left unmodified.
